newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Nov corporate bond issues to hit 6-yr high.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Nov corporate bond issues to hit 6-yr high.

text.p: South Korean companies plan to issue a total of 3.1 trillion won worth of corporate bonds in November, the highest in six years, the Korea Securities Dealers Association said on Thursday.
The previous record was 2.92 trillion won worth issued in January this year, the association said in a report.
The amount includes plans by four companies to issue 60 billion won worth of convertible bonds, the report said.
Bond dealers said yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds have been rising recently due to speculation that new issues would sharply rise in November.
The three-year yields closed Wednesday's session at 12.08 percent, up from the previous close of 12.05 percent.
